claim: The optimal aggregation strategy for per-step uncertainty scores in LLM agent fault detection varies by method and benchmark, making aggregation a hidden hyperparameter that can produce arbitrarily large performance differences without changing the underlying uncertainty signal.
falsifier: On a new method and benchmark, evaluate multiple aggregation strategies (product, average, last, etc.) and observe whether the best strategy differs; test whether tuning aggregation can invert method rankings.

conditions: Observed across methods (UAM, proposed method) and benchmarks (ALFWorld, REAL, WebShop)
Product excels on ALFWorld, average excels on REAL, average/last excel on WebShop for the proposed method
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported methods, benchmarks, and aggregation strategies; transfer to other uncertainty signals or tasks is unestablished.

title: Choice of aggregation strategy for Fault-detection performance
